title: Invoices and documents — where to find your records
body:
On the **„Documents”** tab you find all your records in one place: your invoices and the
declarations you accepted when you ordered.

![Screenshot: the Documents tab on a phone](assets/hu/screen.png)

## The two lists

Two buttons at the top of the tab separate the two kinds of document:

- **„Invoices”** — the invoices we have issued to you, with a downloadable PDF.
- **„Contracts”** — what you agreed to: the order details, your acceptance of the General Terms
  and Conditions and your photo rights declaration.

## The invoice list

At the top of the list, a pale box sums up at most four figures:

- **„Issued invoice”** (Invoices issued) — how many invoices have been issued (matching the filter).
- **„Paid so far”** — their total amount. This is **not a debt**: it is the total of the invoices
  already paid, which is why the cell also says "not a debt" underneath.
- **„Amount due now”** (Currently payable) — what you need to settle NOW. If every invoice is paid,
  it shows 0 and below it "all issued invoices settled". If it is not zero, your website
  may be suspended because of it — settle this first. (Only visible with a subscription.)
- **„Next renewal date”** — when the next fee is due.

Important: if you filter by year, the invoice count and the "Paid so far" amount switch to that year
(the first cell's heading then names the year). This way you see exactly what you need to give your
accountant. "Currently payable" and the renewal date do not depend on the filter.

## What a row shows

The **top, bold line of a row tells you WHAT the invoice is for** — for example
**„Website subscription”** (Website subscription — followed in brackets by the payment rhythm: yearly or monthly) or
**„Multilingual website — one-time generation fee”**. Below it, in pale text, is the **invoice number**, and
next to it the **invoice date**; for a renewal also **the period the invoice covers**
(for example "28. 08. 2026 – 27. 09. 2026"). The amount is on the right.

It is built like this because many of your invoices may have similar amounts, and the invoice number alone
would not tell you which one was for what. With the item name you can pick out the one you need at a glance.

## Downloading an invoice

Every row has a **„PDF”** button — one tap, and the invoice downloads.
You can forward it to your accountant.

If a row shows **„Billing in progress”** with the **„No document yet”** tag,
the invoice is still being issued. In this case the item name is in the pale line below the label,
because this row has no invoice number yet. This is not an error and there is nothing for you to do:
as soon as it is ready, it appears here, and we also send it to you by email.

## Searching and filtering

In the search field you can type the **item name** (for example "multilingual"), the **invoice number**, the
**amount** or the **period** — the list narrows down immediately. It also finds matches without accents:
"szamla" finds "számla". Next to it are year buttons; these only ever offer the years
that really have documents.

If you have filtered, the **„Clear filter”** link appears, which brings back the full list.

If your search also has matches in the other list, the screen says so next to the number of matches,
and one tap takes you there. You do not have to search for the same thing twice.

## Contracts

These entries cannot be changed — their very purpose is to keep a record of what you agreed to
and when. Where we also stored the text, you can read word for word what you
accepted.
